en overvejelse.explanation: "En overvejelse" means "a consideration". It is the noun for the verb "at overveje" (to consider). To say something happened after some thought, use the plural: "efter nogle overvejelser" (after some consideration).

en ovn.explanation: "En ovn" means "an oven". To say you turn it on, use "at tænde" (to turn on): "Jeg tænder ovnen" (I turn on the oven). For the cooking surface on top, use "en kogeplade" (a stovetop) instead: "Jeg koger vand på kogepladen" (I boil water on the stovetop).

et offentligt rum.explanation: "Et offentligt rum" means "a public space". After "i det" (in the), the adjective ends in "-e": "i det offentlige rum" (in public space). The word "et rum" can also mean "a room": "Lejligheden har tre rum" (The apartment has three rooms).

et offentligt toilet.explanation: "Et offentligt toilet" means "a public restroom". The adjective ends in "-t" here, but it ends in "-e" after "det" (the): "det offentlige toilet" (the public restroom).

et offer.explanation: "Et offer" means "a victim". To talk about someone hurt in a crime, say: "Politiet talte med offeret" (The police spoke with the victim). It also means "a sacrifice". To say something costs you something you give up, say: "Det kræver et offer" (It takes a sacrifice).

et omdømme.explanation: "Et omdømme" means "a reputation". It is built from "om" (around) and "at dømme" (to judge). To say something harms it, use "at skade" (to damage): "Skandalen skadede firmaets omdømme" (The scandal damaged the company's reputation).

et omklædningsrum.explanation: "Et omklædningsrum" means "a locker room". It is built from "omklædning" (changing clothes) and "et rum" (a room).

et område.explanation: "Et område" means "an area". When you talk about a subject someone knows well, it means "a field": "Hun er ekspert på dette område" (She is an expert in this field).

et ophold.explanation: "Et ophold" means "a stay". It comes from the verb "at opholde sig" (to stay somewhere). It is also in "en opholdstilladelse" (a residence permit).

et opholdsrum.explanation: "Et opholdsrum" means "a lounge". It is built from "et ophold" (a stay) and "et rum" (a room). Do not mix it up with "en stue" (a living room), which is in a home: "Vi sidder i stuen" (We are sitting in the living room).

et opkald.explanation: "Et opkald" means "a phone call". When you mean the talk itself, use "en samtale" (a conversation): "Vi havde en lang samtale" (We had a long conversation). To name a call nobody picked up, say: "et ubesvaret opkald" (an unanswered call).

et opkøb.explanation: "Et opkøb" means "an acquisition / buyout". It comes from "at købe op" (to buy up). To talk about a takeover the owners did not want, say: "et fjendtligt opkøb" (a hostile takeover).

et oplæg.explanation: "Et oplæg" means "a presentation / proposal". To say someone gives a talk, use "at holde" (to hold): "Han holder et oplæg om klima" (He gives a presentation about climate).

et oprør.explanation: "Et oprør" means "a rebellion / uprising". To say someone refuses to obey, use "at gøre oprør mod" (to rebel against): "Børnene gjorde oprør mod reglerne" (The children rebelled against the rules).

et opslag.explanation: "Et opslag" means "a post", as on social media: "Hun skrev et opslag om sin ferie" (She wrote a post about her vacation). To talk about a paper notice on a wall, use it too: "Der hænger et opslag på skolen" (There is a notice up at the school).

et optog.explanation: "Et optog" means "a parade". To say people march together in one, use "at gå i optog" (to walk in a parade): "Børnene går i optog" (The children march in a parade).

et ord.explanation: "Et ord" means "a word". It is the start of compounds such as "en ordbog" (a dictionary, literally a word book). To say you keep a promise, use "at holde" (to keep): "Jeg holder mit ord" (I keep my word).

et ordforråd.explanation: "Et ordforråd" means "a vocabulary". It is built from "ord" (word) and "et forråd" (a stock of supplies), so it is literally a stock of words. To say someone knows many words, say: "Hun har et stort ordforråd" (She has a large vocabulary).

et ordspil.explanation: "Et ordspil" means "a pun / wordplay". It is built from "et ord" (a word) and "et spil" (a game), so it is literally a word game. To say you made one, say: "Jeg lavede et ordspil" (I made a pun).

et ordsprog.explanation: "Et ordsprog" means "a proverb". To give a well-known Danish one: "Den, der intet vover, intet vinder" (Nothing ventured, nothing gained).

et organ.explanation: "Et organ" means "an organ", as in a part of the body. To talk about an authority, it also means "a body": "et offentligt organ" (a public body).

et overblik.explanation: "Et overblik" means "an overview". It is built from "over" (over) and "et blik" (a look). To say you have lost your grip on things, say: "Jeg har mistet overblikket" (I have lost track of things).

et overfald.explanation: "Et overfald" means "an assault". It comes from the verb "at overfalde" (to attack). If the attacker also steals something, use "et røveri" (a robbery) instead: "Der var et røveri i banken" (There was a robbery at the bank).

et overskud.explanation: "Et overskud" means "a surplus". In a company's accounts, it means the profit left after costs: "Regnskabet viser et overskud på en million" (The accounts show a surplus of one million). To say you have energy to spare, use "at have overskud" (to have energy to spare): "Jeg har ikke overskud i dag" (I do not have the energy today).

et overskæg.explanation: "Et overskæg" means "a mustache". It is built from "over" (over) and "et skæg" (a beard), so it is the beard hair above the mouth.
